wins.label: Strong Investment Banking growth
wins.evidence: Firm-wide IB fees were up 18% year-on-year, reflecting particular strength in underwriting fees

wins.label: Robust net inflows across wealth management
wins.evidence: strong net inflows across AWM as well as in the CCB and Wealth Management business

wins.label: Solid profitability and capital position
wins.evidence: net income of $13.4 billion, EPS of $4.44 on revenue of $42.5 billion and delivered an ROTCE of 21%

wins.label: Consumer financial health remains resilient
wins.evidence: Consumers remain financially healthy, supported by a resilient labor market. While cash buffers have largely normalized, balances were still above pre-pandemic levels

wins.label: Card business momentum with 13% outstandings growth
wins.evidence: Card outstandings were up 13% due to strong account acquisition and the continued normalization of revolve

risks.label: Deposit margin compression ongoing
risks.evidence: deposit margin compression and lower deposit balances in CCB. Migration from checking and savings to CDs is sort of the dominant trend that is driving the increase in weighted average rate paid

risks.label: Markets revenue volatility and pullback risk
risks.evidence: Markets revenue was down $400 million or 5% year-on-year. some meaningful portion of that is likely pulling forward from later in the year

risks.label: M&A advisory headwinds from regulatory environment
risks.evidence: Advisory business still faces structural headwinds from the regulatory environment. there's the well-known kind of regulatory headwinds there, and that's definitely having a bit of a chilling effect

risks.label: Macro and geopolitical uncertainties persist
risks.evidence: economic, geopolitical and regulatory uncertainties that we have been talking about for some time remain prominent. I just think the chance of that happen is higher than other people

risks.label: Credit normalization and charge-off increases
risks.evidence: Net charge-offs were up $116 million predominantly driven by Card. net charge-offs were up $825 million year-on-year predominantly due to continued normalization in Card
